second_order: rallying people to build, repair and defend the flag
theme_note: These codes all recruit, join, repair or defend the Czech work; they vary from first calls and late arrivals to alarms, refresh instructions and direct hands-on repair.

second_order: working out the flag's borders, wedge and proportions
theme_note: These codes work out how a common flag can be made legible and coordinated; what varies is the border, colour, slope, sequence and difficulty of the plan.

second_order: putting beer, hearts, words and Czech pictures on the canvas
theme_note: These codes propose, make or refine recognisably Czech additions; they vary among beer, hearts, words, mottos, maps, cartoons and other pictures.

second_order: choosing whom to invade, erase or spare
theme_note: These codes choose or dispute a target for expansion or erasure; positions vary from calls to invade to restraint, disguise and objections that someone else's work would be destroyed.

second_order: asking neighbours for help and paying help back
theme_note: These codes request, answer, promise or repay help between groups; they vary in whether aid is for a flag, repair, defense, relocation or an alliance being honored.
These codes bargain over crowded canvas room with smaller neighboring works; they vary among borders, moving, transparency, apology, refusal and reciprocal protection.

second_order: making, doubting and repairing pacts with neighbours
theme_note: These codes make and test relations with neighboring groups; they vary among truces, votes, diplomats, warnings, distrust, denial of rogue attacks and plans brought back from elsewhere.

second_order: building and defending Czech-Slovak roads and shared work
theme_note: These codes build or defend work explicitly shared with Slovakia, especially D2 and the Czechoslovak highway; they vary from design and relocation problems to defense and border hearts.

second_order: taking coordination to Discord, polls and dedicated threads
theme_note: These codes move or concentrate coordination in named venues; they vary among Discord, polls, a dedicated subreddit, private-message access and the moderator's megathread redirects.

second_order: using bots to hold or remake the work
theme_note: These codes describe people using automated placement or adapting work around it; they vary between overnight repair, mutual bot use and declaring a manual proposal too late against scripts.

second_order: explaining r/place to people arriving late
theme_note: These codes make the event intelligible to people who missed or still did not understand it; they vary from a direct answer to bewilderment after many posts or even after the ending.

second_order: thanking neighbours and celebrating shared work
theme_note: These codes thank participants or turn completed joint work into friendship and celebration; they vary among foundation thanks, alliance praise, shared jokes, songs and post-event gratitude.

second_order: trying to carry the flag into r/place copies
theme_note: These codes try, report or dispute carrying r/place into replacement canvases; they vary from sharing an all-year copy to recruiting, rejecting repetition and painting a new flag.
These codes use accusation, historical provocation or personal mockery across group boundaries; they vary from framing claims and national taunts to insults over whose work matters.

second_order: marking the end and looking back at the canvas
theme_note: These codes announce, document or personally assess the finished event; they vary among correcting ending images, sharing a timelapse, congratulating people and calling the event procrastination.
